newsitem.title: UK: UK says no need to continue with Channel 4 funding.
newsitem.headline: UK says no need to continue with Channel 4 funding.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade & Industry said on Monday that the current government funding formula used to run Channel 4 would end from 1999.

"There is neither need nor reason for the Channel 4 funding formula to continue now that the channel is well established and successful," the DTI quoted British culture secretary Chris Smith as saying.
Smith said there was no need, or real justification for the C4 formula now that it was a well-established broadcaster with a steady income stream.
Smith said he welcomed a move by Independent Television Commission to agree to a new licence for C4. He said he expected the licence would be in place by the end of the year.

Channel 4 was founded in 1982 and was orginally financed by a levy on the advertising revenue of all of Britain's commercial independent television companies. In return, the companies sold Channel 4's advertising time and kept the proceeds.
But in 1993, Channel 4 became a public corporation, licensed and regulated by the ITC and funded by selling its own advertising time.
